claims.text: Selecting X = Al in CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of a stable, coherent protective oxide layer above 900 °C.
Selecting X = Si in CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of a stable, coherent protective oxide layer above 900 °C.
Al-containing alloys form Al2O3 during high-temperature oxidation.
Si-containing alloys form SiO2 during high-temperature oxidation.
Al2O3 and SiO2 are slow-growing, low-oxygen-diffusivity oxides under the stated conditions.
The Al2O3 or SiO2 scales adhere well to the CrFeCoNiX substrate.
Low oxygen diffusivity and slow oxide growth produce a coherent, adherent protective scale.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX forms oxides with higher oxygen diffusivity than the oxides formed by the Al- or Si-containing alloys.
Mn-containing oxide scales have a thermal-expansion mismatch with the substrate.
Mn-containing oxide scales exhibit phase instability under the stated exposure conditions.
High diffusivity, thermal mismatch, and phase instability in Mn-containing scales cause loss of adhesion, cracking, and spallation.
The nanoscale structure, composition, and oxide–substrate interfacial coherence govern oxide-layer stability.
Al- and Si-containing alloys will retain continuous, stable, adherent oxide layers during exposure above 900 °C.
The Mn-containing alloy will develop less coherent oxide scales that crack or spall and expose the underlying metal.
The proposed comparison applies to CrFeCoNiX alloys in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states at temperatures above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Behavior may differ at lower temperatures or in different exposure atmospheres.
